title: Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (Exam PL-300)
description: Industry-recognised credential that proves you can prepare, model, visualise and secure data in Power BI using Power Query and DAX. A strong first goal for analysts and BI developers who build reports for business stakeholders.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep material; proctored exam approx. US$165 (price varies by country)
prerequisites: Familiarity with Power BI Desktop, Power Query and basic DAX is expected

title: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate (Exam DP-700)
description: Validates the skills to ingest, transform, secure and monitor analytics solutions in Microsoft Fabric using SQL, PySpark and KQL. Suited to engineers who build lakehouses, warehouses and pipelines for analytics teams.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep material; proctored exam approx. US$165 (price varies by country)
prerequisites: Working knowledge of SQL and PySpark; basic KQL helps

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Fundamentals (Exam DP-900)
description: Entry-level credential covering core data concepts: relational and non-relational data, transactional versus analytical workloads, and the Azure services that support them. Ideal for newcomers moving into data roles or working alongside data teams.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep material; proctored exam approx. US$99 (price varies by country)

title: Intro to SQL
description: Short, hands-on course that teaches how to query relational data with SQL, with exercises that run in the browser on real datasets. A quick way for analysts and scientists to get productive with SELECT, joins and aggregations.
costDetails: Free with a free Kaggle account; certificate of completion on finishing

title: Data Analysis with Python Certification
description: Project-based curriculum that teaches data analysis in Python with NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and Seaborn, ending in certification projects. Best for people who know basic Python and want a free, structured route into data work.
costDetails: Completely free, including freeCodeCamp's own certification (not an industry exam)
prerequisites: Basic Python programming

title: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
description: Nine-course programme that takes complete beginners through data cleaning, analysis and visualisation with spreadsheets, SQL, Python and Tableau, finishing with a capstone case study. Gives a shareable certificate of completion, not an exam-based industry certification.
costDetails: Coursera subscription (about US$49/month in the US, free trial available); total cost depends on how fast you finish
prerequisites: None; no degree or prior experience required

title: Get started with Microsoft Fabric
description: Eight-module learning path that tours Fabric end to end: lakehouses, data warehouses, Real-Time Intelligence, data science, SQL databases and semantic models. A good map of the platform before choosing a specialism or a Fabric exam.
costDetails: Free on Microsoft Learn; a Fabric trial or tenant is needed for the hands-on labs
prerequisites: Basic data concepts and terminology (data engineering, modelling, analysis)

title: Guy in a Cube (YouTube channel)
description: Long-running channel by Microsoft data experts with short, practical videos on Power BI, Fabric, DAX and report design, plus coverage of new releases. Handy for quickly solving a specific problem or keeping up with monthly updates.

title: SQLBI (YouTube channel)
description: Deep-dive videos from the SQLBI team on DAX, tabular data modelling, performance tuning and Power BI best practice. Aimed at practitioners who already build semantic models and want to go further.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Power BI and basic DAX

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals (Exam AI-901)
description: Entry-level Microsoft credential covering core AI concepts, machine learning, computer vision, language and generative AI, plus hands-on use of Microsoft Foundry. It replaces the older AI-900 exam and is a sensible first AI certification for technical beginners.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep material; proctored exam approx. US$99 (price varies by country)
prerequisites: Conceptual AI knowledge, basic Python syntax and familiarity with Azure resources

title: Microsoft Certified: AI Business Professional (Exam AB-730)
description: No-code credential showing you can use generative AI tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents to draft, analyse and decide faster in everyday business work. Well suited to non-technical staff who live in Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint and Excel.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep material; proctored exam fee varies by country (confirm on Microsoft Learn before booking)
prerequisites: Everyday use of core Microsoft 365 apps; no coding needed

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate (Exam AI-103)
description: Role-based credential for developers who plan, build and deploy generative AI and agent solutions with Python and Microsoft Foundry, including vision, text analysis and information extraction. It is the current path for engineers who would previously have taken AI-102.
costDetails: Proctored exam; fee varies by country (associate-level Microsoft exams are typically approx. US$165); study guide is free
prerequisites: Python development experience and familiarity with Azure and generative AI concepts

title: Machine Learning Specialization
description: Three-course specialisation led by Andrew Ng that teaches supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks and practical ML advice with Python. Earns a certificate of completion rather than an industry exam credential.
costDetails: Coursera subscription (about US$49/month in the US); certificates require payment and completing the graded assignments
prerequisites: Basic coding (loops, functions, conditionals) and high-school maths

title: Claude 101
description: A practical starter course on using Claude in day-to-day work, from a first conversation and writing clearer prompts to projects, artifacts, skills and connected tools. Suits anyone in the business who is new to Claude and wants a quick, role-agnostic introduction.
costDetails: Free; sign in to save progress and receive the completion credential

title: AI Fluency: Framework and foundations
description: Teaches a four-part framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) for working with generative AI effectively and responsibly, with a grounding in how large language models behave and where they fall short. Useful for every employee, whichever AI assistant they use.
costDetails: Free; sign in to save progress and take the final assessment

title: Building with the Claude API
description: A long, hands-on developer course covering the Claude API end to end: conversations, system prompts, prompt evaluation, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt caching, MCP and agent workflows. Aimed at engineers who will ship AI features into production applications.
costDetails: Course is free; an Anthropic API key is needed for the exercises and API usage may incur charges
prerequisites: Proficiency in Python, basic JSON handling, and access to an Anthropic API key

title: AI Foundations
description: An introductory, self-paced course on how AI and ChatGPT work, built around a real task you already do. Covers clear instructions, supplying context, reviewing outputs and using AI responsibly, with no technical background needed.
costDetails: Free; sign in with a ChatGPT account to enroll. Badge needs an assessment score of 80% or higher
prerequisites: A ChatGPT account and a real work task to practise on

title: Applied AI Foundations
description: Follow-on course that turns one-off prompts into repeatable workflows: you pick a recurring task, break it into steps, decide where ChatGPT helps and add review points. Best for staff who already use AI occasionally and want to apply it more consistently.
costDetails: Free; sign in with a ChatGPT account to enroll. Badge needs an assessment score of 80% or higher
prerequisites: Some experience with AI tools; completing AI Foundations first is recommended

title: Get Started with Codex
description: Developer course on using OpenAI's Codex coding agent for well-scoped work in a real repository: giving it the right context, setting completion criteria, verifying changes and producing evidence for review. Includes a guided hands-on lab and suits engineers new to Codex.
costDetails: Free; sign in with a ChatGPT account to enroll. Badge needs an assessment score of 80% or higher
prerequisites: Experience working in repositories with an IDE and version control; familiarity with shell commands, tests, builds, pull requests and diffs

title: Build foundational generative AI skills
description: Four-module path that explains how generative AI works, how to use it responsibly, and how to get value from Microsoft Copilot Chat through better prompts and features like Pages and agents. A practical AI-literacy starting point for any employee.
costDetails: Free on Microsoft Learn; some features depend on your Copilot licence
prerequisites: Familiarity with accessing and using Microsoft 365

title: Machine Learning Crash Course
description: Google's free, modular introduction to machine learning covering regression, classification, data preparation, neural networks, embeddings, large language models, production systems and ML fairness. Good for developers and analysts who want solid ML foundations.
prerequisites: Basic Python and introductory algebra/statistics are helpful

title: Generative AI for Beginners
description: Open-source 21-lesson course from Microsoft Cloud Advocates that teaches how to build generative AI applications, from prompt engineering and RAG to function calling, agents and responsible use. Each lesson mixes concepts with code samples in Python and TypeScript.
costDetails: Free and open source (MIT); LLM API usage for the labs may incur cloud costs
prerequisites: Basic Python or TypeScript; access to an LLM API such as Azure OpenAI or Microsoft Foundry

title: Prompt Engineering Guide
description: Free, regularly updated reference on designing prompts for large language models, covering techniques such as few-shot, chain-of-thought and RAG, plus agents, risks like prompt injection, and example prompts. Useful as a bookmark for both business users and developers.
costDetails: Reference guide is free; the publisher also sells separate paid courses

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero (YouTube playlist)
description: Code-along lecture series that builds neural networks from scratch, from backpropagation through language models up to a GPT-style transformer. Aimed at engineers and data scientists who want to understand how modern LLMs actually work.
prerequisites: Solid Python and basic calculus

title: Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Fundamentals (Exam PL-900)
description: Entry-level certification that checks you understand what each Power Platform product does, how Dataverse and environments fit together, and how Power Automate and Copilot Studio agents are used. A sensible first credential for anyone joining an automation project.
costDetails: Free Microsoft Learn prep and practice assessment; exam fee applies (price varies by country, see the exam page)
prerequisites: None

title: Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Developer Associate (Exam AB-400, replaces PL-400)
description: Developer-level certification for people who extend Power Platform with code, custom connectors, Power Automate expressions, integrations and agentic AI. The exam moved from PL-400 to AB-400 on 16 October 2026, so new candidates should book AB-400.
costDetails: Exam fee applies (price varies by country, see the exam page); Microsoft Learn training for AB-400 is not yet listed on the credential page, use the official study guide
prerequisites: Hands-on Power Platform development experience (JavaScript, JSON, TypeScript, C#, REST APIs, Azure)

title: Microsoft Certified: AI Agent Builder Associate (Exam AB-620)
description: Associate certification for builders who design and integrate custom agents in Copilot Studio, including multi-agent designs, MCP servers, connectors, computer use and agent testing. The nearest current Microsoft credential to the retired Power Automate RPA exam for AI-led automation work.
costDetails: Exam fee applies (price varies by country, see the exam page); free study guide and practice assessment on AI Skills Navigator
prerequisites: Experience configuring Copilot Studio agents, plus working knowledge of Power Fx, Dataverse, generative AI concepts and REST APIs

title: Microsoft Applied Skills: Create and manage automated processes by using Power Automate
description: Hands-on credential where you prove in a timed interactive lab that you can build cloud flow triggers, notification actions, conditional logic, approvals and sharing. A practical, lower-cost way to evidence core Power Automate skills.
costDetails: Applied Skills assessments are free; lab can be retaken after a 72-hour wait
prerequisites: Familiarity with Power Platform and Power Automate

title: Microsoft Applied Skills: Enhance agents with autonomous capabilities
description: Lab-assessed credential covering how to give a Copilot Studio agent knowledge, agent flows as tools, event triggers for autonomous behaviour, and error handling with human hand-off. Good for people linking Power Automate flows to agents.
costDetails: Applied Skills assessments are free; lab can be retaken after a 72-hour wait
prerequisites: Experience building basic Copilot Studio agents; working knowledge of Power Automate and Dataverse

title: Microsoft Power Automate Essential Training
description: A concise instructor-led course covering connectors, triggers, actions, conditions and approvals, building flows from templates, mobile flows, and creating and troubleshooting flows with Copilot. Good for staff who want a structured, certificated introduction to cloud flows.
costDetails: Requires a LinkedIn Learning subscription; a 1-month free trial is offered
prerequisites: None

title: Power Automate - Complete Guide to Power Automate Desktop
description: A long, hands-on Udemy course dedicated to desktop flows, taking learners from the basics through to building working RPA automations. A good paid option for anyone who needs to automate desktop and legacy applications.
costDetails: One-off Udemy purchase; price varies and is often discounted
prerequisites: Windows PC; no prior RPA experience needed

title: Mastering Microsoft Power Automate 2026: From Zero to Hero
description: A broad Udemy course covering the Power Automate interface, connectors, flow types, variables, conditions, loops, HTTP actions and AI integration, built around the newer flow designer. Suits people who want one paid course that spans cloud flows end to end.
costDetails: One-off Udemy purchase; price varies and is often discounted
prerequisites: None

title: Introduction to RPA with Power Automate Desktop
description: A 21-module on-demand course on building desktop flows, covering variables, conditions and loops, Excel, web, file and PDF automation, best practice, troubleshooting, and combining desktop flows with cloud flows. Suits newcomers to RPA who want a structured path with a completion certificate.
costDetails: Listed on the Pragmatic Works Free Community plan; paid plans also exist, so confirm the certificate is included on the free tier
prerequisites: Windows PC with Power Automate for desktop

title: Demonstrate the capabilities of Microsoft Power Automate
description: Short beginner path introducing cloud and desktop flows, triggers and actions, and then building, testing, monitoring and sharing a first cloud flow. Ideal starting point for non-technical staff.
prerequisites: None

title: Build and optimize cloud flows in Power Automate
description: Beginner path that moves from a first flow into expressions, run-after error handling, HTTP connectors and troubleshooting slow flows. Useful for builders who want their flows to be dependable rather than just working in a demo.
prerequisites: None

title: Create and Manage Automated Processes by using Power Automate
description: Intermediate path on approval flows, flows that manage user information and flows across multiple data sources, ending in a guided project. It is the official preparation route for the matching Applied Skills assessment.
prerequisites: Basic Power Platform and Power Automate knowledge

title: Desktop flows and Robotic Process Automation in Power Automate
description: Ten-module path on Power Automate for desktop: flow control, variables, parameters, loops, recording, scripting, web automation and exception handling. Suits anyone moving from cloud flows into UI-based RPA.
prerequisites: Experience building cloud flows

title: Get started with process mining in Power Automate
description: Beginner path covering the process mining web portal, the Process Mining desktop app and Power BI reporting so you can find bottlenecks before deciding what to automate. Handy for analysts doing discovery work.
costDetails: Hands-on exercises need the Power Automate process mining add-on (trial or licence)
prerequisites: Basic business process knowledge

title: Automate and Extend Your Solutions with AI in Microsoft Power Automate
description: Recently updated path on event-driven cloud flows, Dataverse triggers and actions, approval flows, and AI Builder grounded prompts that answer questions from your own Dataverse data. Good bridge from classic automation into AI-assisted flows.
prerequisites: Completion of the Dataverse data model learning path or equivalent; a Power Automate account

title: Microsoft Power Automate documentation
description: The official reference hub for cloud flows, desktop flows, process mining, Copilot features, solutions and ALM, administration, connectors and troubleshooting. Worth bookmarking as the first stop when something does not behave as expected.

title: Automation adoption best practices overview
description: Microsoft's guidance for setting up and scaling an Automation Centre of Excellence, with articles on strategy, the HEAT lifecycle, governance, managing Power Automate for desktop at scale and an automation maturity model. Useful when advising clients on roll-out and governance.

title: Power Platform Well-Architected
description: Architecture guidance built around five pillars (reliability, security, operational excellence, performance efficiency and experience optimisation), with design checklists and a self-assessment tool. Helps architects review Power Platform and Power Automate workloads before go-live.
prerequisites: Working Power Platform solution experience

title: Power Automate for Beginners
description: A 38-video playlist from a well-known Microsoft Power Platform presenter that walks through building cloud flows step by step, with practical SharePoint, Excel, Forms and approval scenarios. A solid free starting point for business users and new makers.
prerequisites: Microsoft 365 account with Power Automate access

title: Power Automate Advanced Tutorial
description: An 18-video playlist from a UK-based Microsoft solution architect covering the harder parts of cloud flows such as XPath for nested arrays, solutions and deployment, and converting cloud flows to agent flows. Suits people who already build flows and want to make them faster and more robust.
prerequisites: Comfortable building cloud flows with expressions and solutions

title: Power Automate Desktop for Beginners | From Zero to Hero
description: A short free playlist introducing Power Automate Desktop, including web application automation, Excel handling and string functions. Useful as a quick first look at desktop flows (RPA) before committing to a longer course.
prerequisites: Windows PC with Power Automate for desktop installed

title: Workflow Automation with Microsoft Power Automate (3rd edition)
description: A December 2025 book by Aaron Guilmette covering cloud flows, desktop flows (RPA), AI Builder and Copilot, plus governance, compliance and enterprise deployment. A useful reference for consultants designing automations for clients.
costDetails: eBook listed at around 32 USD on Packt; paperback and Packt subscription access also available
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with Microsoft 365

title: Power Automate Forum - Microsoft Power Platform Community
description: The main community Q&A forum for Power Automate, where makers and Microsoft staff discuss problems, known issues and workarounds for cloud and desktop flows. Worth bookmarking for troubleshooting and for spotting issues before they hit a client project.
costDetails: Reading is free; posting requires signing in with a Microsoft account

title: Power Automate - Microsoft Power Platform Blog
description: Microsoft's official blog feed filtered to Power Automate, carrying product announcements, general availability news and monthly Power Platform feature updates. Worth following to keep client advice current as the product changes.

title: GitHub Foundations (Exam GH-900)
description: Entry-level credential that proves you understand Git, repositories, pull-request collaboration, project boards, security features and the wider GitHub community. A good first milestone for developers, testers and non-developers who work in GitHub every day.
costDetails: Proctored exam fee (approx. US$99, varies by country); free practice assessment and study guide; no renewal required
prerequisites: None; some hands-on use of GitHub is recommended

title: GitHub Actions (Exam GH-200)
description: Validates the ability to design, secure and troubleshoot CI/CD workflows with GitHub Actions, including writing custom actions and managing Actions at organisation scale. Suits engineers who automate build, test and release pipelines.
costDetails: Proctored exam fee (approx. US$99, varies by country); free practice assessment; valid for 2 years
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Git/GitHub and basic CI/CD concepts

title: ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL v4.0)
description: The most widely recognised software-testing qualification, covering test fundamentals, testing across the lifecycle, static testing, test design techniques, test management and tooling. Ideal for testers, QA engineers and developers who want a shared testing vocabulary.
costDetails: Exam fee set by national ISTQB board / exam provider and varies by country; syllabus is free to download; optional paid training courses
prerequisites: None

title: Meta Front-End Developer Professional Certificate
description: Nine-course programme from Meta covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, version control, UX basics and a capstone project, finishing with a shareable Coursera certificate. Suits career-changers or upskillers who prefer a guided, video-led path with graded work.
costDetails: Coursera subscription (7-day free trial, then monthly fee; courses can be audited free without the certificate)
prerequisites: None

title: The Odin Project - Full Stack Web Development
description: Open-source, project-based curriculum that takes you from HTML and CSS through JavaScript, React, Node.js and databases while you build a portfolio. Best for self-motivated beginners who want a structured full-stack route without paying.
costDetails: Free, community-funded; no certificate is issued
duration: Self-paced; typically several months at 10-15 hrs/week
prerequisites: None

title: GitHub Skills
description: Short, hands-on courses that run inside your own GitHub repository and give feedback via GitHub Actions, covering pull requests, merge conflicts, Pages, Actions, Copilot and more. Great for learning real GitHub workflows by doing.
costDetails: Free on public repositories; no certificate is issued
duration: Self-paced; most courses take 30-60 minutes each
prerequisites: A free GitHub account

title: Write your first code using C# (Get started with C#, Part 1)
description: Four short modules that introduce C# syntax, variables, basic maths and if/else decision logic using in-browser exercises. A friendly starting point for anyone heading into .NET back-end development.
costDetails: Free; earns Microsoft Learn achievement badges, not a certification
prerequisites: None

title: Learn web development (MDN Web Docs)
description: Mozilla's structured guide to the core front-end skills: HTML, CSS layout, JavaScript, accessibility, version control and an introduction to frameworks, with extension modules on async code, testing and server-side work. A reliable reference to keep bookmarked at any level.
costDetails: Free; no certificate
prerequisites: None

title: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
description: Concise, practitioner-written guides on secure coding topics such as authentication, session management, input validation, injection and XSS prevention, plus framework-specific advice for .NET, Node.js, Docker and Kubernetes. Handy for code reviews and secure design discussions.
costDetails: Free, open-source; no certificate
prerequisites: Working knowledge of at least one programming language

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (Exam AZ-900)
description: Entry-level Microsoft credential covering cloud concepts, core Azure compute, networking and storage services, and Azure management and governance. The usual starting point for anyone in IT, business or development who will work with Azure.
costDetails: Free learning paths and practice assessment; proctored exam approx. US$99 (varies by country)
prerequisites: None; basic IT familiarity helps

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (Exam AZ-104)
description: Role-based associate credential for people who deploy and run Azure environments, spanning identity and governance, storage, compute, virtual networking and monitoring. A core certification for cloud and infrastructure engineers on a Microsoft stack.
costDetails: Free learning paths and practice assessment; proctored exam approx. US$165 (varies by country); free annual online renewal
prerequisites: Experience with PowerShell or Azure CLI, networking, virtualisation and Microsoft Entra ID

title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (Exam AZ-305)
description: Expert-level credential on designing Azure solutions for identity, governance, data storage, business continuity and infrastructure, aligned to the Well-Architected and Cloud Adoption frameworks. Aimed at experienced architects and senior engineers turning business needs into designs.
costDetails: Free learning paths and practice assessment; exam approx. US$165 (varies by country); requires Azure Administrator Associate first; free annual online renewal
prerequisites: Azure Administrator Associate certification (AZ-104) and experience in Azure administration, development and DevOps

title: AWS Cloud Solutions Architect Professional Certificate
description: Four-course AWS-authored programme on designing and building cloud solutions on AWS, ending in a shareable Coursera certificate and helping prepare for the Solutions Architect Associate exam. Useful for engineers who want structured AWS architecture training alongside their Azure skills.
costDetails: Coursera subscription (monthly fee, free trial may apply); the AWS Solutions Architect Associate exam (approx. US$150) is a separate purchase
prerequisites: Basic IT and cloud familiarity

title: Fundamentals of Terraform on Azure
description: Introduces infrastructure as code with Terraform on Azure: declarative syntax, variables, outputs, loops and reusable modules, with Azure CLI and VS Code exercises. A practical first step for engineers who want repeatable, version-controlled deployments.
costDetails: Free on Microsoft Learn; an Azure subscription (free trial available) is useful for the hands-on work
prerequisites: Familiarity with Azure resources and resource groups is recommended, not required

title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials
description: AWS's free self-paced introduction to cloud concepts, core AWS services, security, pricing and support, built to prepare learners for the Cloud Practitioner exam. Useful for anyone who needs a broad grounding in AWS before working with it, whatever their technical role.
costDetails: Free digital course with a free AWS Skill Builder account (hands-on labs and the Cloud Practitioner exam, approx. US$100, are separate); no certificate for the course itself
duration: Self-paced; roughly 6-13 hours depending on edition
prerequisites: None

title: Introduction to Kubernetes (LFS158)
description: Free course explaining Kubernetes architecture, core building blocks such as Pods, Services, volumes, ConfigMaps and Ingress, and how to run a local cluster with Minikube. A solid foundation before moving to CKA-style hands-on work.
costDetails: Free with a Linux Foundation account; 90-day access; a digital badge is available but it is not a certification
prerequisites: Some Linux administration knowledge helps but is not required

title: TechWorld with Nana (YouTube channel)
description: Well-known channel by Nana Janashia with clear walkthroughs of Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Terraform and wider DevOps topics, including long full-course videos. Good for visual learners who want practical explanations to complement formal study.
costDetails: Free on YouTube; paid bootcamps and courses are offered separately by the creator
duration: Self-paced; many videos from 15 minutes to several hours
prerequisites: None

title: Azure Architecture Center
description: Microsoft's library of reference architectures, design patterns, technology decision guides and example workloads aligned to the Well-Architected and Cloud Adoption frameworks. An essential reference for designing secure, resilient Azure solutions.
costDetails: Free documentation; no certificate
prerequisites: Working knowledge of core Azure services

title: Project Management Professional (PMP)
description: The global benchmark credential for people who lead projects, covering predictive, agile and hybrid delivery across people, process and business-environment domains. Suits experienced project and delivery managers who want a widely recognised professional credential.
costDetails: Exam fee roughly US$400-575 depending on PMI membership, plus required 35-hour training course; confirm current fees on pmi.org
duration: Typically 2-4 months of preparation; exam is 180 questions in 240 minutes
prerequisites: Several years of experience leading projects (varies by education level) plus 35 hours of project management education, or a CAPM certification

title: Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)
description: PMI's entry-level credential that proves you understand project management fundamentals, predictive and agile approaches and business analysis. A good first step for project coordinators, junior project managers and career changers.
costDetails: Exam fee roughly US$225-300 depending on PMI membership, plus 23 hours of education if not already completed; confirm on pmi.org
duration: Exam is 150 questions in 3 hours; allow 4-8 weeks of preparation
prerequisites: Secondary school diploma or equivalent and 23 hours of project management education before the exam

title: Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I)
description: An online assessment validating your understanding of the Scrum framework and the Scrum Master accountabilities. Well suited to Scrum Masters, delivery leads and team members who want a respected, lifetime credential.
costDetails: Assessment US$200 per attempt; optional Scrum.org training courses cost extra
duration: Self-study then a 60-minute, 80-question online assessment (85% pass mark)
prerequisites: None formally; working knowledge of the Scrum Guide is expected

title: Google Project Management Professional Certificate
description: A seven-course programme covering project initiation, planning, risk, execution, agile and Scrum, with a hands-on capstone. Suits beginners moving into project coordination or management, and counts towards the education hours needed for PMI's CAPM.
costDetails: Coursera subscription, about US$49 per month after a 7-day trial in the US/Canada; included with Coursera Plus
duration: ~140 hours; about 6 months at 10 hours per week
prerequisites: No prior experience or degree required

title: Project management: the start of the project journey
description: A free taster of postgraduate study that explains what projects are, how they begin, feasibility and decision-making, project life cycles and the project manager's main tasks. Useful for newcomers who want a solid grounding before choosing a methodology or certification.
costDetails: Free statement of participation on completion

title: Project governance and Project Management Office (PMO)
description: A short free course on how governance works around projects, the roles of boards, sponsors and managers, and how different kinds of PMO are set up. Helpful for delivery managers and anyone working with or building a PMO.
costDetails: Free statement of participation on completion
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with project work is helpful

title: Foundations of Project Management
description: The first course of the Google Project Management certificate, introducing project roles, methodologies, project life cycles and the day-to-day work of a project manager. A friendly starting point for anyone with no prior experience.
costDetails: Free to start; the graded certificate experience needs a Coursera subscription (availability of no-certificate access may vary)

title: The 2020 Scrum Guide
provider: Scrum Guides (Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland)
description: The official, short definition of Scrum covering the theory, values, team accountabilities, events and artifacts. Essential reading for anyone working in or alongside Scrum teams, and the main source for Scrum.org and Scrum Alliance exams.

title: The Agile Coach
description: A free library of practical articles and tutorials on agile, Scrum, Kanban, backlogs, sprints and how to run them in Jira. Ideal for teams new to agile ways of working or choosing between frameworks.

title: Lenny's Podcast
description: Long-form interviews with leading product and growth people on how they build, prioritise and lead products. Best for product managers and product owners who want real-world practice and career insight.
costDetails: Also available on podcast apps

title: CMI Level 3 Diploma in Management (Combined)
description: A UK-regulated qualification for supervisors and first-line managers, covering leading and managing individuals and teams. A good route for new team leads who want a formal, recognised management qualification.
costDetails: Fees set by CMI-approved training centres; contact a centre for current prices
duration: 550 hours total qualification time; pace set by the training centre
prerequisites: Typically a supervisory or team-leading role; delivered through an approved centre

title: CMI Level 5 Management and Leadership (Award, Certificate, Diploma)
description: CMI's benchmark qualification for middle managers, with Award, Certificate, Diploma and Extended Diploma sizes. Suits practising or aspiring department and operations managers and is a stepping stone towards Chartered Manager status.
costDetails: Fees set by CMI-approved training centres; contact a centre for current prices
duration: Award 40, Certificate 130, Diploma 370 hours total qualification time; pace set by the centre
prerequisites: Management experience or an aspiring manager role; delivered through an approved centre

title: ILM Level 7 Strategic Leadership and Management
description: A postgraduate-level ILM qualification for senior leaders preparing for or working in executive roles, covering organisational strategy, innovation and performance. The ILM page also lists the Level 3 and Level 5 routes for earlier-career managers.
costDetails: Fees set by ILM-approved training providers; contact a provider for current prices
prerequisites: Senior management or executive-level responsibility is expected; delivered through an approved ILM centre

title: Leading People and Teams Specialization
description: A five-course specialisation on inspiring and motivating individuals, managing talent, influencing others and leading teams, finishing with a capstone project. Suits new and aspiring managers who want structured, certificated learning.
costDetails: Coursera subscription or Coursera Plus; financial aid may be available
duration: ~56 hours; about 4-6 months at a few hours per week
prerequisites: No prior experience required

title: Leadership and followership
description: An eight-week free course on leadership styles, key leadership skills, common mistakes and how leaders grow their followers, including a week on emotional intelligence. Good for anyone who wants to understand leadership, not just people with a title.
costDetails: Free statement of participation and free digital badge on completion
duration: ~24 hours over 8 weeks (about 3 hours per week)

title: Effective communication in the workplace
